acquisition method: The Q Exactive was run in DDA-MS2 top10 method with full MS spectra collected at a resolution of 70,000, a scan range of 300 to 1750 m/z and an AGC target of 3 × 106 or 20 ms maximum injection time.
alkylation reagent: Chloroacetamide was then added at 1 in 100 dilution and incubated for 1 hour on a rotating platform at room temperature.
alkylation concentration: Chloroacetamide was then added at 1 in 100 dilution and incubated for 1 hour on a rotating platform at room temperature.
cleavage agent: Cell lysates were quantified and mixed in a 1:1:1 ratio for each SILAC experiment and digested with Lys-C and trypsin.
enrichment method: seven SCX fractions were phospho-peptide enriched using titanium dioxide beads to enable the identification of occupied serine, threonine and tyrosine phosphorylation sites.
fractionation method: Peptides were then separated into fractions using strong cation exchange chromatography (SCX)
instrument: Samples were analysed by LC-MS/MS on a Q-Exactive Orbitrap mass spectrometer in biological triplicate
labeling: stable isotope labelling by amino acids in cell culture (SILAC)
Modulation of cell signaling following inhibitor treatment was quantified using global phosphoproteomics and stable isotope labelling by amino acids in cell culture (SILAC)
reduction reagent: 1 mM Dithiothritol was then added to this mixture and incubated for 1 hour on a rotating platform at room temperature.
reduction concentration: 1 mM Dithiothritol was then added to this mixture and incubated for 1 hour on a rotating platform at room temperature.
